posts.title: A Quieter Glass of Water: Designing the Shizuku Countertop Filter
posts.excerpt: In our Rotterdam workshop, we set out to build a countertop filter that respects the morning routine through honest materials, steady gravity, and simple care.
posts.content:
When we founded Shizuku Filter in 2023 at Harbour Lane 14 in Rotterdam, our workshop had a single guiding question: why have kitchen water filters become such loud, complicated plastic appliances? Most countertop solutions involve noisy motorized pumps, intrusive plumbing lines, or disposable synthetic pitchers that rattle on a refrigerator shelf. We wanted to build something quieter and more durable. Our goal was to create one thoughtful product—the Shizuku Countertop Filter—combining a matte stone-grey ceramic housing, a 1.6 L clear glass carafe, and an unhurried four-layer cartridge that relies on natural gravity rather than electricity.

From the earliest sketches, Ines Okoro focused on proportions that would sit comfortably on a narrow kitchen counter. Measuring 14 × 14 cm at the base and 32 cm tall, the filter occupies minimal workspace while holding 2.1 kg of solid, stable weight. Priya Raman refined the stone-grey ceramic body through repeated slip-casting trials, ensuring the matte surface wipes clean with a damp cloth and resists kitchen stains. Sitting neatly beneath the ceramic housing is a removable 1.6 L carafe blown from clear glass. The carafe was shaped specifically to balance easily in the hand, whether you are pouring a morning kettle or filling a bedside tumbler.

Inside the housing rests our four-layer cartridge, engineered by Tomas Lindgren to condition everyday tap water without inflated promises. Water first passes through a ceramic pre-filter to catch coarse sediment, then through granular activated carbon to reduce harsh municipal chlorine smells, an ion-exchange resin to soften water and reduce kettle limescale, and finally a fine mesh that catches loose media. We make no medical claims or exaggerated percentage statistics. Instead, we focus on what matters at the table: clearer water that tastes fresh and clean. The entire 1.6 L carafe fills in about 4 minutes, producing a gentle, quiet trickle that aerates the water naturally.

To test the filter before scaling production, we built an initial batch of 50 pilot units for testing in genuine households across three European cities. In Rotterdam, the Verhoeven family of four kept the filter on their central kitchen counter through weeks of busy breakfasts. In Lisbon, a design studio of nine people used it daily to brew morning tea and keep water carafes at hand without disturbing their shared workroom. In Hamburg, Amira, a hospital nurse working night shifts, relied on the filter for calm hydration in her small flat without disturbing neighbours with noisy plumbing. Their reports confirmed that each cartridge delivers about 2 months or 150 L of dependable filtration.

Now, our 21-day campaign runs from 3 November to 23 November 2026 to fund our tooling and first production run. Backers have pledged $31,480 toward our $40,000 goal, with 412 backers supporting our work and 12 days left to take part. Mateo Ruiz has scheduled tooling validation for December 2026, followed by our structured 50-unit pilot run in January 2027 and mass manufacturing in February and March. All backer rewards ship directly from our workshop in April 2027, backed by Hana Kowalski and Leo Brandt's bi-weekly progress updates. We look forward to delivering a calmer glass of water to your home.
